label: v4.0.9
profile_release:
[profile.release]
opt-level = 3
lto = "fat"
codegen-units = 1
panic = "abort"
strip = "symbols"

# release-native inherits release; the per-host-CPU specialization is
# applied via RUSTFLAGS="-C target-cpu=native" in .cargo/config.toml
# (always on for the Linux toolchain). Build artifacts produced under
# this profile are NOT portable across CPU classes — they target the
# build host. By project policy users compile from source for their CPU.
cargo_config:
[build]
jobs = 50

# Default to a portable modern microarchitecture (x86-64-v3 = SSE4.2 +
# AVX2 + BMI2 + FMA, ~2013 Haswell+; aarch64 stays at the toolchain
# default). Avoids SIGILL in CI when binaries built on one runner's CPU
# class are reused on a runner with fewer features (sccache cross-host),
# and avoids surprising end users who consume published binaries on a
# different CPU class. Hot SIMD lanes still use runtime `is_x86_feature_
# detected!` dispatch (vector kernels, key-compare, JSON tokenize) so
# AVX-512 / etc. above v3 still light up when present.
#
# Local devs who want full per-host optimization (and accept that the
# resulting binary is not portable to other CPUs in their fleet) can
# opt in via:
#   RUSTFLAGS="-C link-arg=-fuse-ld=mold -C target-cpu=native" cargo ...
# or the `release-native` cargo profile (defined in workspace Cargo.toml)
# which inherits this base + relies on env-supplied RUSTFLAGS for the
# CPU upgrade.
[target.x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu]
linker = "clang"
rustflags = [
    "-C", "link-arg=-fuse-ld=mold",
    "-C", "target-cpu=x86-64-v3",
]

[target.aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu]
linker = "clang"
rustflags = [
    "-C", "link-arg=-fuse-ld=mold",
]
sandbox: standalone git clone --no-local under .agent/sandbox, removed after the build
